title: Two New England beach towns to visit before the summer ends
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, Cape Cod named the best town by Boston.com readers, offers beaches, oyster specials, and sunset cruises.
Ogunquit, Maine, voted the best beach town in New England, is highlighted for its scenic beauty and attractions.
Provincetown's Chach Restaurant announces closure on Nov. 3 after 21 years, prompting social media tributes.

title: Diver dies in incident off Cape Cod
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 72-year-old man died in a diving incident off Cape Cod near Sesuit Harbor on Wednesday.
Dennis Fire Department, along with multiple agencies, coordinated efforts to recover the missing diver.
The incident involved marine and aerial units, and it remains under investigation according to authorities.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues after graphic testimony about children’s autopsies
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial continues with graphic testimony on autopsies, causing her to sob in court.
Massachusetts State Police testified about Clancy's internet searches on psychiatric care and suicide methods.
Clancy admits to strangling her children; defense argues mental illness exempts her from criminal responsibility.

title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: The 2,724 sq ft Westerly, Rhode Island beach house features a contemporary cottage style and was built in 1987.
The property includes three bedrooms, three full bathrooms, and offers water views on both sides.
2025 taxes for the beach house are $11,125, with a listing price quiz showing options of $1.78 to $1.98 million.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (August 13, 2026)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: First Crush, a natural wine bar, will open in mid-September at 259 Washington St., Somerville.
Chef Jeff Almendras to open Filipino-inspired restaurant in Fort Point, featuring tamarind tots and chicken adobo.
Jūni, a sushi restaurant by Chris Chung and Kenny Leung, opens at 1211 Hancock St., Quincy with a ten-seat counter.

title: 3 concerning trends from Red Sox’ 5-game losing skid
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Red Sox have lost five consecutive games, with each loss featuring a potential tying run at the plate or on base.
Boston's offense has declined, averaging 2.8 runs in the last five games compared to 5.6 in a prior 37-game stretch.
Injuries are affecting the bullpen, with Garrett Whitlock battling elbow inflammation and Aroldis Chapman struggling in consecutive games.

title: An Easton church has been converted to a $1.3m home
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: The former Swedish Evangelical Lutheran Church at 16 Williams St., Easton, converted into a home, is listed for $1.3 million.
The 5,730-square-foot residence includes four bedrooms, three-and-a-half bathrooms, and retains original church design elements.
Features include a Viking-equipped kitchen, a great room with stained glass, and a spa-inspired primary suite with a steam shower.

title: Blue Jays erupt for 5 runs in the eighth to beat Red Sox 6-4, extend Boston’s skid to 5
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Toronto Blue Jays scored five runs in the eighth inning to defeat the Boston Red Sox 6-4.
Willson Contreras hit his 24th home run for the Red Sox, who have now lost five consecutive games.
Toronto's Kazuma Okamoto contributed a go-ahead RBI single, and the Blue Jays boosted their wild-card position.

title: Allston-Brighton residents divided over future of Jackson Mann Community Center, survey shows
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Survey shows no clear consensus among 553 respondents on Jackson Mann Community Center redevelopment options in Allston-Brighton.
Options include housing, a school, or both with a community center; 190 support housing, 171 school, 124 both.
Mayor Wu will decide on the center's future by end of year, with further surveys and meetings planned.

title: Tour the Patriots’ new 160,000-square-foot training facility
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots unveiled a 160,000-square-foot training facility, the largest NFL facility solely dedicated to football.
The New Balance Athletics Center features a 15,000-square-foot weight room, virtual reality room, and a spacious locker room with 92 lockers.
The facility includes a hydrotherapy room, dining facilities resembling restaurants, and a player's lounge equipped with recreational amenities.
